subtitle: The day-by-day agenda for the May 1971 Network Working Group meeting, with reading lists of earlier RFCs.

tldr.problem: Attendees of the May 1971 NWG meeting needed to know the schedule, the rooms and which RFCs to read beforehand.
tldr.mechanism: Steve Crocker lists each session with its time, title, relevant RFC numbers and speakers, from short host reports to organization of the group itself.
tldr.outcome: It is a meeting agenda, not a protocol. The unit metadata shows it was updated by RFC 149.

sections.title: Schedule and Rooms
sections.content:
The NWG meeting runs from 8 p.m. on Sunday, May 16 through Wednesday evening, May 19. Most meetings are in the Wicker Room of the Dennis Hotel, and the Sunday evening meeting is in the Royal Box Room. Evening meetings start at 8 p.m., afternoon meetings at 1:30 p.m. and morning meetings at 9 a.m.

The Wicker Room is reserved through Thursday afternoon, and attendees may use it for private meetings when nothing is scheduled.
sections.plainLanguage: It says which days the group meets, which rooms to use and when each part starts.

sections.title: The Sessions
sections.content:
Sunday evening is short reports: each host gives a report of five minutes or less on hardware, NCP, Telnet and applications. Monday morning covers the NIC and the Telnet committee's proposed protocol. Monday afternoon covers file transfer protocols, the TIP, network management and long-range planning, and other ARPA projects.

Monday evening discusses operating systems and networks, with a presentation by Professor Art J. Bernstein on an operating system for a network-embedded computer. Tuesday morning covers the data reconfiguration service and data sharing on computer networks.
sections.plainLanguage: Each session has a topic, like a school timetable: reports, then Telnet, then file transfer, then how operating systems fit in.

sections.title: Technical Matters and Group Organization
sections.content:
Tuesday evening is for remaining technical matters: socket numbers, procedures for testing NCPs and Telnets, ways to experiment with protocol, the initial connection protocol and remaining glitches in the second level protocol. RFC 129 is among those listed for reading.

Wednesday evening is non-technical. The author says the group has grown and changed in two years and is perhaps not optimally organized for technical work, so the meeting will consider what to expect by the end of 1971 and how the group should be organized and managed.
sections.plainLanguage: The last sessions fix leftover problems and then ask how the club itself should be run now that it has grown big.

references.text: RFC 113, listed for Sunday evening and Wednesday evening.
